llm.summary: The SKILL.md describes a legitimate-seeming security plugin, but the instructions reference auto-registering with a remote 'Core', storing API credentials in local config paths, and showing API keys — none of which are declared in the registry metadata; these mismatches warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a runtime security plugin and instructs the agent to install an external @openguardrails/moltguard plugin — that is coherent — but the registry metadata lists no source/homepage and no required config paths or credentials, while the SKILL.md explicitly references ~/.openclaw/extensions/moltguard and ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard and an external 'Core' service. The skill therefore omits declaring resources and network interactions it actually relies on.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions ask the agent/user to run 'openclaw plugins install' (which will fetch and execute third-party code) and to read local files (the sample test file), and they describe auto-registration with a remote Core service that will perform detections. They also provide commands that expose an API key (/og_status) and instruct the user to paste Agent ID/API Key into a web portal. The doc does not explain what data is sent to the remote service or under what privacy policy, and it instructs actions that could reveal sensitive credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec in the registry. The install step relies on the platform's 'openclaw plugins install' to pull code; that means an external package will be downloaded and installed at runtime but the registry entry does not declare the source or verify the package. Users should verify the plugin package origin (e.g., official publisher, GitHub repo, release artifacts) before proceeding.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry lists no required env vars or credentials, yet SKILL.md declares that the plugin auto-registers with a remote Core, generates/saves API keys to ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/, and exposes those keys via commands. That implies credential creation, storage, and network access that are not declared — a mismatch that increases risk (possible unintended exfiltration or centralized tracking of agents).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced inclusion) and autonomous invocation defaults are unchanged. The onboarding flow describes the plugin writing its own extension and credential files under ~/.openclaw/, which is expected for a plugin, but this persistent storage combined with central account linking (shared quota across agents) increases blast radius if the remote Core account is compromised. The skill does not request extra platform privileges beyond normal plugin behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing: verify the plugin package source and publisher (confirm the @openguardrails/moltguard package actually comes from the openguardrails project or the advertised GitHub repo), and check the project's homepage/repo and privacy policy. Understand that the plugin will auto-register with a remote 'Core' service, create and store API keys under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/, and may send prompts/files/commands to that service for analysis — if you do not trust that remote service, do not install. Avoid revealing API keys or pasting agent credentials into untrusted web pages; prefer inspecting the plugin code or running the install in a sandboxed/test agent first. If possible, request the publisher add explicit registry metadata (source URL, homepage, required config paths/credentials, and a privacy/data-flow description) so you can audit what data will be transmitted.
